title: Which of these six numbers does eleven divide?
description: Six numbers are tested for eleven in turn. For each, the digits on the one more places are added, the digits on the other places are added, and one total is taken away from the other. A zero or a multiple of eleven means it divides, and any other total is read as a remainder, with a minus total turned into a remainder by adding eleven.
teaching_notes: One idea: excess take away short is zero or a multiple of eleven when eleven divides the number, and otherwise it gives the remainder. Watch for students who give a minus total as the remainder, or who sort the places from the left instead of from the units.

source: A Shortcut for Divisibility by 11: test and find remainders
video_script.why: A learner uses the excess and short shortcut on six numbers, and meets zero, a multiple of eleven, a positive total and a minus total.

video_script.payoff_line: The remainders are four, five, eight and seven, and the last two numbers are divisible.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the shortcut for eleven, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='excess'/>Add the digits on the units, hundreds and ten thousands places. This total is called the excess.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Add the digits on the tens, thousands and lakhs places. This total is called the short.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take the short away from the excess. Zero or a multiple of eleven means eleven divides the number.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>Any other total gives the remainder. A minus total is short, so we add eleven to it.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Given, six numbers: one hundred fifty eight and eight hundred forty one.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Then four hundred eighty one and five thousand five hundred twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Last, ninety thousand nine hundred four and eight lakh fifty seven thousand seventy six.

beats.on_screen: To find: is each number divisible by 11? If not, the remainder

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which numbers eleven divides, and the remainder for the others.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, take one hundred fifty eight. The excess is eight plus one, which is nine. The short is five.
<bookmark mark='r1'/>Nine take away five is four, so the remainder is four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Take eight hundred forty one. The excess is one plus eight, which is nine. The short is four.
<bookmark mark='r2'/>Nine take away four is five, so the remainder is five.

marks.minus: 5 − 8 = −3 is written and read as 3 short

narration: <bookmark mark='sums'/>Step two, take four hundred eighty one. The excess is one plus four, which is five. The short is eight.
<bookmark mark='minus'/>Five take away eight is minus three, which is three short.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add eleven to minus three and we get eight, so the remainder is eight.
<bookmark mark='excess'/>Step three, take five thousand five hundred twenty nine. The excess is nine plus five, which is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The short is two plus five, which is seven.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Fourteen take away seven is seven, so the remainder is seven.

marks.m22: 22 is ticked as a multiple of 11
marks.both: 22 and −11 are ticked as multiples of 11

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step four, take ninety thousand nine hundred four. The excess is four plus nine plus nine, which is twenty two. The short is zero.
<bookmark mark='m22'/>Twenty two is a multiple of eleven, so eleven divides it.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Take eight lakh fifty seven thousand seventy six. The excess is eleven and the short is twenty two.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Eleven take away twenty two is minus eleven, which is a multiple of eleven. Eleven divides it too.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Step five, put the answers back. Eleven times forty three is four hundred seventy three, and adding eight gives four hundred eighty one.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Eleven times eight thousand two hundred sixty four is ninety thousand nine hundred four.
